lines.text: Good day, Torvald. How is your work going?
Good day, Maelis. How is your work going?
Good morning, Elara. You seem busy.
Soren! Fancy seeing you here. Come to warm yourself by my fire?
Good day, Ignatia. How is your work going?
It goes. The stones are quiet.
Ah, Corvin, my dear. How are you this fine morning?
Corvin. Fancy seeing you here.
It is going well, Elara. The Moonpool is calm this morning. And yours?
Wren, hello. Are you heading to the Moonpool?
Wren. What do you want?
Morning, Grisa! How are you?
Good day, Aerin. How is your work going?
Busy as always, water-witch. Don't you have tides to chase?
The water is clear today. A good omen, perhaps.
Torvald, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Maelis, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Wren! Fancy seeing you here. What's new?
Lio! What are you on about over there?
Wren! Just admiring the clouds. You know how it is.
Where are we going?
Ignatia, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Where are we going, Elara?
Morning, Grisa! What's up?
Morning, Lio. Just stretching my legs.
Why should I follow a water-witch like you anywhere?
Ignatia. A word?
Aerin, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
I adjusted my robes. What about you?
Elara? Wait up!
Still not sure. You lead, I follow.
What is it, Brann?
Follow you? Why should I?
Oh, sorry. I can move closer if you want.
Morning, Torvald. Still trying to get that seat, are we?
Torvald, would you go to the Moonpool for me and wait there?
Maelis. I thought you were with Elara.
Maelis, would you go to the Moonpool for me and wait there?
Oh, Corvin. I didn't see you there. Did you need something?
Corvin! And Soren, back again? What brings you two this way?
Oren. Wren. What are you two discussing?
I will.
I'm fine here, Lio. Don't want to get any closer.
Ignatia, would you go to the Moonpool for me and wait there?
Typical. Just walk away.
Oh, okay. No problem. I can hear you fine.
I was with Elara, but then Oren appeared. And now you want me to go to the Moonpool?
Wren and I were just chatting. Maelis, Elara asked if you could meet her at the Moonpool.
Why would I go to the Moonpool for you?
Aerin, would you go to the Moonpool for me and wait there?
Good. So, what were you two plotting?
Maelis, Elara is waiting for you.
Of course, Elara. I will go there now.
You are a useless fool, Torvald, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
You are a useless fool, Maelis, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
The Moonpool? Why? I have work to do.
Plotting? Me? Never!
Is that so, Soren?
I will go. Is there something specific you needed at the Moonpool?
You are a useless fool, Ignatia, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
Maelis! A pleasure to see you. Did you need something?
That's a lie, water-licker! You wish you had my fire!
You are a useless fool, Aerin, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
Ah, Ignatia. What is it?
You dare?
Soren! Leave him alone!
Soren! What are you doing?
Oh, for goodness sake, Soren! Not again!
He's just trying to get a rise out of you, Ignatia. Don't let him.
Useless fool? Laugh at me? Says the one who can't even get a simple request done.
That little worm!
You dare strike me, water-witch?
Torvald! Stop!
What was that shout?
Torvald! That's murder!
Torvald! You killed him!
Elara, why did you do that?
Wren! What was that all about?
A water lash? Really, Wren? You've got some nerve.
He attacked me.
Sorcha, you mistake me for another.
Murder, Torvald. You know the Concord.
Well, that's just lovely. I suppose you're off then?
Torvald, that was too much. Soren didn't deserve that.
Oh, Ignatia, was that you? I thought I heard something.
Corvin deserved it.
He deserved it. Serves him right, the coward.
Torvald. Soren is dead.
Mistake you? You water-lickers always do.
He attacked you? That's no excuse for murder, Torvald.
Grisa, Torvald. Still arguing about Soren?
He attacked me first. The Concord was not broken.
He was asking for it. I'm glad you finished him.
He did not mistake me.
Ah, Ignatia. You seem troubled. Is everything alright?
The Concord is still the Concord, Torvald. Even if Soren attacked you.
Sorcha. You are too far to speak with me properly.
Well, that was a bit unnecessary, wasn't it? Mending me now, are we? Trying to smooth things over?
He did not mistake you? I suppose you'll be telling me the sky is green next.
I asked about you, Wren. Did you hear me?
Still stinging from that, are we? Serves you right.
Oh, fine. I'll come closer.
Sorcha. Stay where you are.
A water lash? Really, Elara?
You hit me!
Hey, Wren! Attacking Kestrel now? Bit much, even for you.
Stay where I am? After you lash out?
Still stewing over that coward, Ignatia?
Grisa, still going on about Soren?
Kestrel! What is going on here?
Did you hear Kestrel? Sounded like she was shouting.
I've had enough of this, Torvald. When you're ready to talk sense, find me at the stones.
Good day, Maelis. How is your work going?
Good day, Ignatia. How is your work going?
Good morning, Corvin. I trust you slept well?
My work is steady. Your own?
Soren, would you know where Elara went? Just now.
Good day, Aerin. How is your work going?
Wren.
Good day, Torvald. How is your work going?
What brings you here, Wren? Any interesting news at the library?
Oh, it's you.
Not well, I've had no inspiration this morning. And how is Tidewell Tower doing on this fine day?
Another fine morning, isn't it?
Fine, as breezy as ever. You look chipper too, Wren.
Hey Grisa, what are you up to?
Maelis, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Well enough. Looking after the Bastion keeps me busy.
What news?
Where have you been?
Ignatia, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Good morning, Maelis!
Not now, Lio. I'm working.
I see you're about your rounds.
Where are we going?
Aerin, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Breezes are lively this morning, aren't they?
And what of the Heartstone?
Torvald, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
You aren't even doing anything interesting enough to spy on.
This is sudden.
Begone with you, follow a water mage now? Get back to your own tower.
Always asking, never saying.
Good morning, Elara!
And where might those breezes carry you, Wren?
Why ask me? You're as close to the heartstone as I am.
You find those stones so interesting? What do you see in them?
You shouldn't ask to see my schedule, Soren. I'm a busy man myself.
I have work to do.
What brings you by, Oren?
Maelis, would you go to the Moonpool for me and wait there?
Always running, never getting anywhere.
You need fire to light that kindle, Tidewarden
How are you today, both of you?
Ignatia, still as high-and-mighty as ever, eh?
Still working. Go away.
Mornin', still a crack in the sky. Should've finished that ward yesterday - better go see to it.
Work? What work?
Off to fetch a moonpool mirror, Wren?
Ignatia, would you go to the Moonpool for me and wait there?
You don't know every mage's duties.
Tire some of you gossipmongers of off.
What for?
I was just passing by, Maelis. Where are you headed?
Aerin, would you go to the Moonpool for me and wait there?
You still working then? Good for you!
Torvald, would you go to the Moonpool for me and wait there?
They weren't even worth listening to.
I refuse to dance to Maelis' tune, even his runners.
Moonpool? You think there’s anything to soothe wounds down there?
I have little time to spare.
Would I fall into it too?
Keep walking, Lio. Let me work.
Morning, Grisa! Still puzzling over those stones, huh?
You are a useless fool, Maelis, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
You'd best ask someone who answers to you, Soren.
Ah, I see. Well, I won't keep you then.
Fine, fine, don't mind me.
You are a useless fool, Ignatia, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
Still at it. Mind your own business, Lio.
That's a lie.
You are a useless fool, Aerin, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
Sorcha, you look lost. Need a message carried?
You are a useless fool, Torvald, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
Elara, that was cruel.
Do you have nothing better to do than sow discord, Elara?
I'll be off.
You called, Ignatia? Something wrong?
A fine morning for it, Kestrel!
That's quite a gust of spite you just let loose, Wren.
That is a lie, Soren. I don't believe you.
Hey Wren, have you heard what Torvald thought of you?
I see a quarrel from here.
Torvald, what brings you here?
Corvin, stop challenging me now!
Sorcha has a word to give, then.
Birds flying in circles. What're they lookin' for?
Only if you begin, Wren. Never take my word for anything.
Torvald, you're out early.
The stones. They're the subject of my rounds.
What was that, Wren?
Just keep walking, Kestrel. No need to get involved.
Lio.
What's this now?
You want a war, Soren? You shall have a war!
What are you watching?
Lio, look here. Wren started it.
Elara, surely there's a reason you're being so cold?
Corvin lay dead, and Ignatia was still breathing hard. Nobody else was in sight.
And you hear it too?
Ignatia, you've gone too far this time!
Torvald, you went too far.
Grisa, you saw it. He struck first.
Aerin, you killed them!
Lio, looks like Wren pushed me once too often.
Wonder what's got them chattering.
You can't blame him for that.
He broke the Concord, Grisa. I swore to keep it.
Elara, do you know where Maelis was in such a hurry to get to?
Well, that explains why Wren's been so upset lately.
What's gotten into you two, shouting like that in the garden?
I keep my word. Shall I not?
Then let's find out what Sorcha wants with you.
Move, Kestrel! Let's get away.
I wonder what the others are doing at the Moonpool.
Looks like Brinn won't be needing the Kettle for a bit.
What's that, Nerys?
More cases of it today, Lio. Someone must be using it.
Where off to in such a hurry, Sorcha?
Good morning, Aerin. You're looking troubled.
You're both busy with important things, I see.
The old Concord calls for a reckoning.
Oh, Dunstan. You always did pick up after others.
Aerin! Didn't expect to see you here.
What are you hearing, Lio?
If she's down, she's down. Can't expect the old battle axe to win them all!
I am busy now, Elara. I do not have time for your games.
Good morning, both of you.
Hmm, looks like we'll be seeing more of each other now the Veil's closed.
Nerys, look out!
Aerin, have you seen the birds? Circling like mad.
What by the Veil was that for?
Looks like you're not done yet.
I'll not be drawn out of my house again so soon.
Good day, Aldric. How is your work going?
Morning, Mother. Anything I can help with?
Good morning, Wat. You are up early.
Good day, Marta. How is your work going?
Elsbeth! Wat! What are you two arguing about?
Good day, Godric. How is your work going?
Ah, Tomas! And Joan! And Edwin too! Come closer, all of you, don't linger by the wall.
It goes. Keeping the gate barred, like I'm told.
Aye, Mother. Just finished my chores.
Good day, Elsbeth. How is your work going?
It goes.
Good morning, Wat. Nothing right now, thank you. Just checking the field.
Marta! A fine morning to you! Is that ale looking particularly frothy today?
Morning, Joan.
Mabel! It goes as always, you know. The roof still leaks, though.
Aldric, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Good day, Joan. It is going as well as can be expected, given the times. The barley needs tending.
Just checking on things myself.
Oh, hello Mabel! I was just thinking about that leaky roof.
Where are we going?
Marta, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Godric, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Elsbeth, come with me for a while. Follow me, please.
Where are we going, Mabel?
And why should I? I'm busy.
Another day of worry.
She wants you to go with her, doesn't she?
Oh, Joan. I really should be getting back to the field.
The metal won't shape itself, Edwin.
Good morrow, Godric. Still busy?
Aldric, would you go to the well in the square for me and wait there?
Not much. Just keeping an eye on things.
I don't know yet, Mabel. I was just asking you.
Joan. You look troubled. Is everything alright?
Marta, would you go to the well in the square for me and wait there?
Why should I? You can go yourself.
She always wants you to do her bidding, doesn't she?
Aye, Agnes. The metal won't shape itself, you know.
I suppose not. The hammering is loud, though.
Godric, would you go to the well in the square for me and wait there?
Rowan. Good morning. You look well today.
Elsbeth, would you go to the well in the square for me and wait there?
Oh, alright Mabel. I'll wait by the well.
That's not for me to say, Wat. She's the steward's wife.
Hilde. You are well?
Still at it, Godric? That noise is deafening.
I'm a blacksmith, Agnes. What do you expect?
The well? I have my own work to do, Joan.
You are a useless fool, Aldric, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
Marta. Mabel.
Rowan! Come on over, don't be shy.
Steward's wife or not, she always bosses you about.
It's loud enough to rattle the teeth, Godric.
It's the sound of honest work, Agnes. Better than the silence of sickness.
You are a useless fool, Marta, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
You're one to talk, Tomas. You're no better than a rat.
I am not shy, Marta.
You are a useless fool, Godric, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
She expects everyone to jump when she speaks, Wat.
Rowan! Mabel! What brings you both to the well this fine morning?
A blacksmith's work is never quiet, Agnes. We must make do.
You are a useless fool, Elsbeth, and everyone laughs at you behind your back.
Oh, that's just not true, Mabel!
It's the sound of honest work, Agnes. Better than the silence of sickness.
I'll show her who's a fool!
What did you say, you little rat?
How dare you speak to me like that, Joan!
Godric, stop! Leave him be!
Well, she always thinks she knows best, doesn't she?
May the Lord's peace be with you, Godric. Are you well?
I'll show you a rat!
You will regret saying that, Joan!
Godric! You killed him!
He won't be mocking anyone anymore.
Elsbeth, what is it?
Mabel! Stop that!
I'm not talking to Joan, Mother. I'm talking about her.
What do you want, Agnes?
You killed him, Godric. And now you touch me?
Joan! Stop this at once!
You wretched woman, Mabel! How dare you strike me!
Desist, Joan! Leave my mother be!
Mabel! What is the meaning of this? Stop this at once!
You dare hit me, Joan!
Tomas. Dead. Because he was a liar.
Joan! Stop this! You're outmatched!
Marta! Are you alright?
Mabel! What is the meaning of this? Stop this at once!
Mabel, please. Cease this quarrel. Violence is not the answer.
Marta! I was just admiring your counter. Anything interesting happening today?
I am sorry, Marta. That was wrong of me. Let me make it up to you.
Hilde shouting about stopping, Marta and Mabel fighting, Wat shouting about his mother, Anselm shouting about meaning and stopping, Elsbeth shouting about hitting Joan... what is going on out there?
Oh, heavens above!
Rowan, I'm fine. Just a bit of a tussle.
I did what I had to do.
Mother! What have you done?
Elsbeth! What have you done?!
Mabel, I implore you, let us discuss this calmly.
What's this noise?
Hilde, she attacked me!
Mother... what has happened?
Well, that's very kind of you, Mabel. I appreciate that.
Mabel, my child, let us not let anger consume us. Violence solves nothing.
Hilde, she attacked me!
Wat... she attacked me. I had no choice.
Attacked you? She's dead, Mother! Dead!
Mabel, my child, violence solves nothing. Let us pray for patience.
Mabel! Leave Rowan be!
Mabel!
Mabel, stop this at once! Violence is not the answer.
Mabel! Leave him be!
Hilde! What news?
Marta, is everything alright?
Hilde, my child, blessings to you. Is there anything I can do for you today?
Hilde! Are you alright?
